1927, May
FR. SOLANUS, NOTEBOOK NO. 1.
Page 37 NOTES ON "FAVORS."
May 19th Consumption Disapears To-day May 19th Miss Hazel Heenan of 149 Davenport St. Detroit reports her Brother Philip out of danger. Said Brother Philip Heenan 45 yrs old examined April 9th by Dr. Williams of Cold Water, Michigan who shows by X-ray consumption positively to be in one lung -- both in rear and front. Shortly before said X-ray he had been enrolled first time and spots seem- ingly healed appeared to be heale ..... enrolled 2nd time and now all appearance of consumption has vanished.
May 23 Fractured Scull Oscar St. Pierre, 23 of Chatham Ont. (BearLine) fell between trolley-cars on April 12th receiving bad fracture of scull. Taken to Hospital he remains unconscious five days, till on the 16th is enrolled perpetually. Comes To-day in perfect condition to thank for prayers, etc. Left Hospital (Hotel Dieu) May 4th Deo Gr!
May 28th Paralysis? Miss Erma Peterson non cath. 20 of 6590 Montererey Ave. Enrolled this evening for Paralisis of whole right side and limbs - weeps with Mother.
May 29 Sunday 1.30 p.m. returns weeping for joy at improvement .. Monday 13th can walk pretty well .... Sunday June 19 says herself: "I can walk very well."
30 Goitre Mrs. Elz Dancy 49 3906 lincoln Enrolled Jan. 18 for terri- ble goitre mostly Inward Operation takes place Jan 24th in Fords. Comes To-day in perfect
June 8th Fr. Stephen. Mrs. Mary Weisner, 10815 E. Jefferson, reports not- able favor through Fr. Stephen Eckert, O.M. Cap.
June 10 11 a.m. Baby Lauraine Timons (3 months old) Reported 107 fever - hopeless, enrolled again this morning - Mother weeping and pray- ing. June 13th 2.30 p.m. "Fever gone but mastoid appearing." 9.15 Child Smiles
11th Awakes after 7 Weeks Sleep. Mrs. George C. Anderson N. Cath 49 (Yrs) 1508 Montclair, received paraletic stroke of the brain October 1st, 1926. An invalide and helpless till February 1st slept for 7 weeks. A Catholic friend enrolled her in S.M.Asso'n Dur last week of March she began to show signs of consciousness. First - Was up and in quite perfect health for Easter and, Thank God, continues so.
